notes: Lopes's narrative was printed in Italian in Ramusio's collection (Venice, 1550); the Portuguese original is lost.

label: Fernandes Pereira
summary: Sailed alone by the outer route east of Madagascar to Cape Guardafui and became the first Portuguese to reach and winter on Socotra.
notes: Some historians date the Socotra discovery to April 1504; route east of Madagascar follows Gaspar Correia.

label: Varthema
summary: First known non-Muslim European to describe Medina and Mecca, travelling with the Damascus Hajj caravan, then explored Yemen from Aden to Sanaa.
notes: Jeddah to Aden by sea. Visit to Sanaa claimed; Taiz assumed on the way back.

label: Varthema in Persia
summary: Travelled inland from Hormuz to Herat and Shiraz with a Persian merchant partner.
notes: Only Herat and Shiraz named; intermediate route conjectural.

label: Tristao da Cunha
summary: Sighted the remote South Atlantic islands that bear his name, then raided the Swahili coast and took Socotra.
notes: Rough seas prevented a landing on Tristan da Cunha. He also raided northern Madagascar (Vohemar and the northwest coast), dates not given.

label: Mascarenes
summary: Sent by Tristao da Cunha to explore around Madagascar, he found Reunion (Santa Apolonia), Mauritius (Cirne) and Rodrigues.
notes: Order of islands and route around Madagascar reconstructed. Group later named Mascarenes after Pedro Mascarenhas (1512).

label: Albuquerque to Hormuz
summary: Followed the Omani coast from Ras al Hadd via Qalhat, Muscat and Sohar into the Persian Gulf to Hormuz.

label: Sequeira
summary: First Portuguese fleet to reach Malacca, after calling on Sumatra's northern ports.
notes: Arrived 11 September 1509; left after a plot against him. Sumatran calls (Pedir, Pasai) reconstructed.

label: Leo Africanus
summary: His Description of Africa, written in Italy and printed by Ramusio in 1550, shaped European knowledge of Timbuktu and the Sahel for centuries.
notes: A Granada-born Muslim diplomat of Fez; included under the Europe viewpoint because his account was written for and published to European readers. Dates c.1510 to 1513 approximate; route via Sijilmasa and Taghaza is the usual reconstruction.

leader: Antonio de Abreu and Francisco Serrao
label: Abreu to Banda
summary: First European fleet to the Banda Islands, following the north coast of Java and the Lesser Sunda chain.
notes: Serrao's ship was wrecked at Sapudi and his replacement junk near the Lucipara islands.

label: Albuquerque to Malacca
summary: Captured Malacca, from which embassies and fleets went to Siam, Pegu, the Spice Islands and China.

label: Fernandes
summary: A Portuguese degredado who walked inland from Sofala to Manica and the Mutapa state, the first European report of the Zimbabwe plateau.
notes: The Wikipedia page read is only a disambiguation line (travelled in Zambia and Zimbabwe, died c.1525). Two journeys c.1511 to 1515; route reconstructed. Wikipedia article could not be fetched in this session (access blocked); route and dates from general knowledge, verify.

label: Serrao to Ternate
summary: Shipwrecked survivors rescued by local rulers were taken into the Moluccas, where Serrao stayed and sent news of the clove islands.
notes: The source only says he was rescued by Moluccan rulers; the route via Hitu (Ambon) to Ternate follows the usual account.

label: Albuquerque Red Sea
summary: First European fleet in the Red Sea; failed to take Aden and reached Kamaran island.
notes: Kamaran stop from general accounts; the source confirms the Red Sea entry and Aden.

label: Jorge Alvares
summary: First Portuguese to reach China by sea, landing at Tamao in the Pearl River delta.
notes: Rafael Perestrello reached the Guangdong coast the same year.

label: Balboa
summary: First Europeans to see the Pacific from the Americas, after crossing the Isthmus of Darien.
notes: Relied on Indigenous guides and more than 1,000 native bearers; reached the Gulf of San Miguel.

label: Piri Reis map
summary: Ottoman world map compiled from Portuguese, Spanish and Columbus charts, showing the Atlantic, West Africa, Brazil and the Caribbean.
notes: Knowledge came second-hand from European charts.

label: Ponce de Leon
summary: First recorded European exploration of Florida's Atlantic coast, Keys and Gulf coast.
notes: Pilot Anton de Alaminos discovered the Gulf Stream on this voyage (general knowledge).

label: Solis
summary: Discovered the Rio de la Plata estuary, opening the way to the Parana and Uruguay rivers.
notes: Killed by local people (probably Guarani) near the Parana-Uruguay confluence.

leader: Fernao Pires de Andrade (with Tome Pires)
label: Andrade to Canton
summary: First official Portuguese mission to China, sailing up the Pearl River to Canton.
notes: Tome Pires's embassy went on overland to Beijing (not plotted here); it ended in imprisonment.

label: Cordoba
summary: First European expedition to the Maya coast of Yucatan, reaching Campeche and Champoton.
notes: Two Maya fishermen seized at Cabo Catoche became interpreters.

label: Grijalva
summary: Followed the Gulf coast of Mexico from Cozumel past Tabasco to Veracruz, bringing first news of the Aztec state.
notes: Fetched page confirms Cozumel and Tabasco; the stretch north of Tabasco is from general knowledge.

label: Cortes
summary: March from the Gulf coast to Tenochtitlan, revealing the Valley of Mexico and the Aztec capital to Europe.
notes: Interpreters Malintzin (Dona Marina) and Geronimo de Aguilar; Totonac and Tlaxcalan allies guided and fought alongside.

label: Magellan
summary: Charted the Patagonian coast and found the strait to the Pacific (Atlantic and strait leg only).
notes: Pacific crossing handled in another region file. Wintered at Puerto San Julian; met Tehuelche people.

label: Pineda
summary: First map of the whole northern Gulf of Mexico coast, from Florida to Veracruz, including the Mississippi mouth.

leader: Francisco Álvares (embassy of Rodrigo de Lima)
label: Álvares
summary: Six-year Portuguese embassy to Lebna Dengel whose printed narrative (1540) gave Europe the first detailed descriptions of Aksum and Lalibela.
notes: Landed Massawa 9 April 1520; met Pêro da Covilhã at court. Intermediate stops (Debre Bizen, Debarwa, Lalibela, Shewa camp) are a reconstruction; the court moved.

label: Magellan
summary: First European crossing of the Pacific, revealing its width, the Marianas and the Philippines, and reaching the Moluccas from the east.
notes: Pacific islands sighted (Puka Puka, Flint) are standard identifications. Pages on the Magellan expedition were blocked; Trinidad page read. Survivors guided in the Philippines by Malay interpreter Enrique.

label: Sequeira Red Sea
summary: Governor's Red Sea campaign that landed the first official Portuguese embassy to Ethiopia.
notes: The embassy of Rodrigo de Lima found Pero da Covilha living at the Ethiopian court. Landing at Massawa from general accounts.

label: Trinidad
summary: Failed attempt by the Trinidad to sail back east across the North Pacific, reaching about 42 or 43 degrees N before scurvy forced a return.
notes: Longitudes of the northern track are not recorded; reconstructed.

label: Alvarado
summary: Conquest route into highland Guatemala and Cuzcatlan (El Salvador).
notes: Thousands of Nahua allies from central Mexico; Kaqchikel at Iximche initially allied.

label: Cortes to Honduras
summary: Overland march across Tabasco and the Peten to Honduras, crossing the Maya lowlands.
notes: Fetched page gives dates only; waypoints (Acalan, Nojpeten, Nito) from general knowledge. Cuauhtemoc executed en route.

label: Gomes
summary: Surveyed the coast from Florida to Nova Scotia for Spain, ascending the Penobscot and naming the Hudson the Rio de San Antonio.
notes: Direction of the coasting (north-to-south or south-to-north) is disputed; plotted south to north.

label: Verrazzano
summary: First survey of the North American Atlantic coast from the Carolinas to Newfoundland, including New York Bay.
notes: Met Lenape people in New York harbour and Wampanoag/Narragansett at Narragansett Bay.

leader: Garcia Jofre de Loaisa; Toribio Alonso de Salazar
label: Loaisa
summary: Second Spanish fleet through the Strait of Magellan; its flagship crossed the Pacific via Bokak atoll and Guam to Mindanao and the Moluccas.
notes: The page read does not name Bokak or Guam; those landfalls are from general knowledge. The Santiago instead sailed north to Mexico.

leader: Francisco Pizarro, Diego de Almagro, Bartolome Ruiz
label: Pizarro voyage
summary: Sailed down the Pacific coast of Colombia and Ecuador to Tumbes, the first European contact with the Inca state.
notes: Fetched page confirms only first contact at Tumbes c. 1528; coastal stops (Gorgona, Santa) from general knowledge.

label: Saavedra
summary: First crossing from Mexico to the Moluccas; its return attempts ran along the north coast of New Guinea to the Admiralties and Marshalls.
notes: Two return attempts (1528, 1529) merged into one track. Specific page listed but not fetched in this session (search budget exhausted); route and dates from compiler's general knowledge.

label: Cabeza de Vaca
summary: Eight-year odyssey of four survivors across Texas and northern Mexico, the first European account of the region.
notes: Route across Texas and Chihuahua is much debated. Companions Andres Dorantes, Alonso del Castillo and Estevanico, an enslaved Moroccan; survived as healers among Indigenous nations.

label: Narvaez
summary: Overland march through northern Florida to Apalachee, then raft voyage along the Gulf coast to Texas.
notes: Raft leg plotted as coastal; Narvaez lost at sea; survivors wrecked near Galveston Island.

label: Pizarro
summary: Conquest route from Tumbes to Cajamarca and along the Inca road to Cusco, opening the Andes to Europe.
notes: Interpreters Felipillo and Martinillo, taken at Tumbes earlier.

label: Belalcazar
summary: From Piura to Quito, then north through the Cauca valley to Popayan, Cali and the Bogota plateau.
notes: Route Piura-Quito and Neiva-Bogota from general knowledge and the El Dorado article.

label: Cartier I
summary: Mapped the Gulf of St Lawrence, Prince Edward Island, Chaleur Bay and Gaspe.
notes: Took Domagaya and Taignoagny, sons of the Stadacona chief Donnacona, who later guided him upriver. Gulf details beyond Gaspe from general knowledge.

label: Almagro
summary: First European expedition into Chile, via the Altiplano and northwest Argentina over the Andes to Copiapo and the Itata.
notes: Andes pass uncertain (San Francisco or Pircas Negras). Return through the Atacama from general knowledge. Thousands of Andean auxiliaries; guide Paullu Inca accompanied.

label: Cartier II
summary: Ascended the St Lawrence to Stadacona (Quebec) and Hochelaga (Montreal); returned by the Cabot Strait.
notes: Guided by Domagaya and Taignoagny; Domagaya's remedy (annedda) saved the crew from scurvy.

label: Federmann
summary: Crossed the Venezuelan and Colombian llanos along the foot of the Andes and climbed to Bogota.
notes: Followed Georg Hohermuth von Speyer's trail and the Muisca salt-trade route.

label: Quesada
summary: Up the Magdalena and onto the Muisca highlands, revealing the Bogota plateau, Tunja and Sogamoso.

label: Mendes Pinto
summary: Adventurer whose Peregrinacao (1614) gave Europe a sweeping, if embroidered, picture of the Red Sea, Malacca, Siam, Pegu, China and Japan.
notes: Accuracy of the Peregrinacao is debated (punned as Fernao Mentes Minto). Route and dates between named regions are highly simplified.

leader: Hernando de Soto (then Luis de Moscoso)
label: De Soto
summary: Four-year march across the American Southeast, crossing the Mississippi and reaching east Texas.
notes: Route follows the Hudson reconstruction in outline (general knowledge); fetched page confirms only the Georgia/South Carolina section. Survivors under Moscoso descended the Mississippi and coasted to Panuco. Juan Ortiz, a Narvaez survivor, interpreted.

label: Ulloa
summary: Showed Baja California to be a peninsula by sailing to the head of the Gulf of California and round to Cedros Island.

label: Grand Canyon
summary: First Europeans at the Grand Canyon, reaching the South Rim near Desert View.
notes: Led there by Hopi guides; Pedro de Sotomayor chronicled.

leader: Joao de Castro (in Estevao da Gama's fleet)
label: Joao de Castro
summary: Expedition to Suez whose Roteiro do Mar Roxo was the first detailed European survey of the Red Sea coasts, with charts and views.
notes: Fleet left Goa 31 December 1540. Intermediate ports (Socotra, Massawa, Suakin, Quseir, El Tor) from the Roteiro's coverage; the source names only Suez and the Sinai shore.

label: Coronado
summary: Searched for Cibola and Quivira, revealing the Pueblo world, the Llano Estacado and the Great Plains as far as Kansas.
notes: Guided onto the Plains by the captive known as El Turco and by Ysopete (Wichita). Pueblo and Plains place names from general knowledge.

label: Valdivia
summary: Marched through the Atacama to found Santiago, then pushed south to Concepcion, Valdivia and Villarrica.
notes: About 1,000 Peruvian auxiliaries; Ines de Suarez accompanied. Killed by Mapuche forces under Lautaro at Tucapel, 1553.

leader: Cristóvão da Gama (account by Miguel de Castanhoso)
label: da Gama in Ethiopia
summary: Portuguese musketeers marched from Massawa through Tigray to Lake Tana's battlefields; Castanhoso's account (1564) described the highlands.
notes: Battle sites (Lake Ashenge area 1542, Wayna Daga 1543) approximate. Wikipedia article could not be fetched in this session (access blocked); route and dates from general knowledge, verify.

label: Orellana
summary: First descent of the Amazon from the Napo to the Atlantic, naming the Rio Negro.
notes: Chronicle by Gaspar de Carvajal. Detached from Gonzalo Pizarro's Canela expedition.

label: Cabrillo
summary: First European voyage along the coast of Alta California, from San Diego Bay to near Point Reyes.
notes: Northernmost point uncertain; recorded Chumash and Tongva villages. Cabrillo died on Santa Catalina 1543.

label: Villalobos
summary: Crossed from New Spain to Mindanao and named the islands Filipinas; Inigo Ortiz de Retes then followed the north coast of New Guinea and named it Nueva Guinea (1545).
notes: Includes the 1545 Ortiz de Retes leg along New Guinea. Specific page listed but not fetched in this session (search budget exhausted); route and dates from compiler's general knowledge.

leader: Antonio Mota and Francisco Zeimoto (Portuguese traders)
label: Portuguese reach Japan
summary: First Europeans to reach Japan, landing on Tanegashima and introducing firearms.
notes: They travelled on a Chinese junk; the starting point and track are reconstructed.

label: Pastene
summary: Naval reconnaissance of the Chilean coast south of Valparaiso to about 41 S.
notes: Southern limit (about 41 S) from general knowledge; fetched page confirms landings near Concepcion and Valdivia.

label: Xavier to Japan
summary: Jesuit mission that landed at Kagoshima, beginning the Jesuit letters that described Japan to Europe.
notes: Guided and interpreted by the Japanese convert Anjiro. Travelled in Japan until 1551.

label: Seydi Ali Reis: fleet
summary: Took the Ottoman Basra squadron out of the Gulf; after battles with the Portuguese off Oman and a storm it was wrecked on the Gujarat coast.

label: Seydi Ali Reis: overland home
summary: Mirat ul-Memalik: overland from Gujarat through Sind, Mughal Delhi, Kabul, Transoxiana and Safavid Iran back to Istanbul.

label: Jenkinson
summary: Englishman who went down the Volga, across the Caspian and the Ustyurt desert via Urgench to Bukhara; his 1562 map of Russia and Tartary followed.
notes: Accompanied by Richard and Robert Johnson. Sellizure identified with Shahr-i Vazir; Kait with Kath.

leader: Pedro de Ursua, Lope de Aguirre
label: Ursua/Aguirre
summary: Descent of the Huallaga, Maranon and Amazon in search of Omagua and El Dorado, ending in Aguirre's revolt in Venezuela.
notes: Exit to the sea disputed: Amazon mouth (plotted) or via the Rio Negro, Casiquiare and Orinoco. Start on the Huallaga from general knowledge.

label: Legazpi
summary: Crossing from New Spain via the Marshalls and Guam to Samar and Cebu, founding the Spanish Philippines.

leader: Andres de Urdaneta; Felipe de Salcedo
label: Tornaviaje
summary: The tornaviaje: first west to east crossing of the Pacific, via the westerlies near 38 N, opening the Manila galleon route.
notes: Landfall at Santa Catalina Island 18 Sep 1565; Acapulco 8 Oct 1565.

label: Mendana
summary: Discovered the Solomon Islands (Santa Isabel, Guadalcanal, Malaita, Makira) and returned via the Marshalls and Wake to Mexico.

label: Barreto on the Zambezi
summary: Portuguese army ascended the Zambezi to Sena and campaigned inland, establishing the river route into Mutapa lands.
notes: Wikipedia article could not be fetched in this session (access blocked); route and dates from general knowledge, verify.

leader: Portuguese Macau to Nagasaki trade ship (nau do trato)
label: Macau to Nagasaki
summary: Portuguese helped found the port of Nagasaki with daimyo Omura Sumitada, the terminus of annual ships from Macau.

label: Frobisher
summary: Entered Frobisher Bay on Baffin Island (1576 to 1578) and in 1578 sailed some way into Hudson Strait.
notes: Three voyages merged; Inuit captives taken to England in 1576 and 1577.

label: Yermak
summary: Cossack raid over the Urals by the Chusovaya, Tagil, Tura and Tobol to Qashliq, capital of the Khanate of Sibir, opening western Siberia to Russia.
notes: 1583 descent of the Irtysh and Ob to Nazym included; drowned in the Irtysh near the Vagai mouth in August 1584 (some sources 1585).

label: Linschoten out
summary: Dutch secretary to the Archbishop of Goa whose Itinerario (1596) published Portuguese sailing directions to the East.
notes: Stops at Madeira, Guinea, the Cape, Madagascar and Mozambique; exact tracks reconstructed.

label: Davis
summary: Charted south-west Greenland and Cumberland Sound, and in 1587 sailed up Davis Strait to 72 12 N (Hope Sanderson).
notes: Three voyages (1585, 1586, 1587) summarised; good relations with Greenlandic Inuit at Godthab fjord.

label: Linschoten home
summary: Return voyage via St Helena and two years on Terceira in the Azores before reaching Lisbon and Enkhuizen.
notes: English corsairs (Drake, Cumberland) disrupted the homeward fleet. Final destination Enkhuizen, plotted at the Texel approach.

label: Lancaster 1591
summary: First English voyage to the Indian Ocean, via Zanzibar and Cape Comorin to Penang and Ceylon.
notes: First recorded British contact with the Orang Asli on the Malay mainland. Only 25 men survived; he landed at Rye in May 1594.

label: Houtman
summary: First Dutch voyage to the East Indies, reaching Bantam, the north Java coast, Madura and Bali.
notes: Stayed about six months on Madagascar (anchorage not named in the source; St Augustine Bay assumed). Pieter Keyser and Frederick de Houtman made southern star observations.

leader: Alvaro de Mendana; Pedro Fernandes de Queiros
label: Mendana 2
summary: Discovered the Marquesas and the Santa Cruz Islands; after Mendana's death Queiros took the survivors to Manila.

label: Raleigh
summary: Ascended the Orinoco via the Manamo channel to the Caroni, producing 'The Discovery of Guiana'.
notes: Chief Topiawari supplied information and guides; his son went to England. Antonio de Berrio had descended the Orinoco in 1590.

label: Barentsz
summary: Discovered Bear Island and Spitsbergen, rounded the north of Novaya Zemlya and survived the first Arctic wintering, escaping by open boat to Kola.
notes: Earlier voyages (1594, 1595) reached the Orange Islands and the Vaygach strait.

label: Houtman to Aceh
summary: Zeeland voyage to Aceh where Cornelis was killed and Frederick imprisoned, later publishing a Malay-Dutch dictionary and southern star catalogue.
notes: Frederick studied Malay during two years of captivity (1599 to 1601). Outbound track reconstructed.

label: Van Neck
summary: Second Dutch fleet; van Neck's ships resupplied on Madagascar's east coast and loaded spices at Bantam.
notes: Madagascar landing place not named in the source. Returned to Amsterdam July 1599 with a full cargo.

label: Warwijck
summary: Part of the second Dutch fleet that landed on and named Mauritius, then sailed via Ambon to Ternate.
notes: Well received at Ternate; back in Amsterdam September 1600.

label: Heemskerck
summary: Reached Great Banda and left 22 men to buy nutmeg, the first Dutch post in the Bandas.

label: Van Neck to China
summary: Brought the first Dutch ships to the China coast, at Macau, where Portuguese forces killed his landing parties.
notes: Departure 1600 and route from Bantam reconstructed; he also fought a Spanish-Portuguese fleet near Ternate on this voyage.

label: EIC first voyage
summary: First East India Company fleet: Table Bay, Antongil Bay in Madagascar, the Nicobars, Aceh, Priaman and Bantam, where the first English factory was set up.
notes: Lemon juice kept the Red Dragon's crew free of scurvy.

label: Goes
summary: Overland from Agra via Kabul, the Pamirs, Yarkand and the Tarim towns to Suzhou (Jiuquan), proving that Cathay was China.
notes: Travelled with the Armenian Isaac, who carried his papers to Matteo Ricci in Peking after Goes died at Suzhou in 1607.

label: Champlain 1603
summary: Re-examined the St Lawrence from Tadoussac to the Lachine rapids.
notes: Gathered Innu, Algonquin and other Indigenous accounts of the Great Lakes.

label: Páez
summary: Spanish Jesuit who settled at Gorgora on Lake Tana and on 21 April 1618 visited the springs of the Blue Nile at Gish Abay.
notes: Arrived Ethiopia 1603. His Historia da Etiópia stayed in manuscript until 1905, but its content circulated through Jesuit writers (e.g. Kircher, Almeida).

leader: Samuel de Champlain, Pierre Dugua de Mons
label: Champlain Acadia
summary: Surveyed the Bay of Fundy and the coast of Maine and Massachusetts as far as Cape Cod.

label: Van den Broecke (Angola)
summary: Dutch merchant whose journal of trading voyages to Cape Verde, Guinea and Angola was published in 1634.
notes: Three trips to Angola between 1605 and 1612, simplified here into one track.

label: Duyfken
summary: First recorded European landfall on Australia, charting the west coast of Cape York in the Gulf of Carpentaria.

label: Queiros
summary: Searched for Terra Australis, crossing the Tuamotus to Taumako and Espiritu Santo (Vanuatu), then returned to Acapulco.

label: Torres
summary: Sailed west along the south coast of New Guinea and through Torres Strait, proving New Guinea was not part of a southern continent.
notes: Account largely suppressed by Spain until the 1760s.

label: Hudson
summary: Sought a polar route: in 1607 along east Greenland to Spitsbergen at 80 N (finding Jan Mayen area waters), in 1608 to Novaya Zemlya.
notes: Specific page listed but not fetched in this session (search budget exhausted); route and dates from compiler's general knowledge.

label: Lake Champlain
summary: Up the Richelieu to the lake later named Lake Champlain.
notes: Travelled with Wendat, Algonquin and Montagnais allies, who guided the war party.

label: Hudson River
summary: Ascended the Hudson River to near Albany, laying the basis for New Netherland.
notes: Fetched page confirms the Hudson ascent to Albany; coastal stops (Penobscot, Cape Cod, Chesapeake, Delaware Bay) from general knowledge.

label: Hudson Bay
summary: Passed through Hudson Strait into Hudson Bay and down the east coast to James Bay.
notes: Wintered near the Rupert River; Hudson set adrift by mutineers June 1611.

label: Button
summary: Crossed Hudson Bay to winter at the Nelson River, then charted the west coast north to about 65 N.

label: Van den Broecke (Aden)
summary: First Dutch merchant in Arabia, at Aden and al-Shihr in Hadramawt, where Dutch traders were left to learn Arabic.

label: Bylot and Baffin
summary: Explored Foxe Channel along Southampton Island, showing no western outlet from Hudson Bay.

label: Champlain Huronia
summary: Via the Ottawa River and Lake Nipissing to Georgian Bay and Huronia, then across Lake Ontario into Iroquois country.
notes: Fetched page confirms the 1615-16 campaign and wintering in Huronia; the canoe route (Ottawa, Nipissing, French River, Trent) is from general knowledge. Wendat guides; Etienne Brule had gone ahead.

label: Baffin
summary: Circuited Baffin Bay, finding Smith, Jones and Lancaster sounds and reaching 77 45 N.

label: Bocarro
summary: Portuguese trader who walked from Tete past the south end of Lake Malawi to Kilwa on the Swahili coast.
notes: Route reconstructed from later summaries. Wikipedia article could not be fetched in this session (access blocked); route and dates from general knowledge, verify.

label: Van den Broecke (Mocha, Surat)
summary: Tried to open a Dutch post at Mocha (where he tasted coffee), then founded the VOC establishment at Surat.

label: Hartog
summary: Landed on Dirk Hartog Island and charted the Western Australian coast north to about 22 S (Eendrachtsland).

label: Le Maire
summary: Opened the Le Maire Strait and Cape Horn route and crossed the Pacific via the Tuamotus, northern Tonga and Futuna to New Ireland and New Guinea.
notes: Specific page listed but not fetched in this session (search budget exhausted); route and dates from compiler's general knowledge.

label: Munk
summary: Danish expedition through Hudson Strait to winter at the Churchill River mouth on Hudson Bay; only three survived.

label: Pyanda
summary: First Russians to reach the Lena, going up the Lower Tunguska and down the Lena towards the site of Yakutsk, returning by the Angara.
notes: Source confirms Pyanda reached the Lena near Kirensk in 1623; the rest of the route is the traditional reconstruction.

label: Carstenszoon
summary: Charted the south coast of New Guinea (sighting its snow peaks) and the east side of the Gulf of Carpentaria to the Staaten River.
notes: Companion ship Arnhem under Willem van Colster crossed to Arnhem Land.

leader: Antonio de Andrade and Manuel Marques
label: Andrade
summary: First Europeans known to enter Tibet, crossing the Mana Pass to Tsaparang, capital of Guge.
notes: Travelled with Hindu pilgrims to Badrinath. The Tsaparang mission lasted until the 1630s.

label: Lobo
summary: Jesuit who crossed the Danakil from Beilul to Tigray, visited the Blue Nile source in 1629 and left via Massawa; his account reached Europe in French (1728) and Johnson's English (1735).
notes: An earlier 1624 attempt via Pate and the Jubba river failed (not plotted).

label: Cacella
summary: First Europeans in Bhutan, continuing over the Himalaya to Shigatse in central Tibet.
notes: Source page could not be fetched in this session (web search budget exhausted); dates and route from general knowledge, check before publication.

label: Thijssen
summary: Charted about 1,500 km of the southern coast of Australia from Cape Leeuwin to the Nuyts Archipelago.

label: Beketov
summary: From Yeniseysk up the Angara and Ilim, over the portage to the Lena, and down it to found the Yakutsk ostrog in 1632.

label: Teixeira
summary: First European ascent of the whole Amazon, to Quito, and back; Cristobal de Acuna's account followed.
notes: Large flotilla with many Indigenous paddlers. Return-trip chronicle by Acuna and route via the Napo from general knowledge.

label: Moskvitin
summary: First Russians to reach the Pacific, by the Aldan, Maya and Ulya rivers to the Sea of Okhotsk.
notes: Guided over the Dzhugdzhur by Evenki knowledge. In 1640 the party also sailed south along the coast towards the Uda and the Shantar Islands and heard of the Amur (not mapped).

label: Perfilyev
summary: Sailed up the Vitim to the Tsipa, the first Russian to enter Transbaikalia (Dauria).
notes: Upper Vitim and Tsipa confluence position approximate.

label: Stadukhin
summary: Down the Indigirka to the Arctic and east along the coast to the Kolyma, where the first ostrog was built.
notes: Dezhnev and Yarilo Zyrian took part; Oymyakon as the start is uncertain.

label: Tasman
summary: Discovered Van Diemen's Land (Tasmania), the west coast of New Zealand, Tonga and Fiji, proving Australia did not join a southern continent.
notes: Tasman page was blocked; route from the maritime exploration page and general knowledge.

label: Poyarkov
summary: First Russian descent of the Amur: up the Aldan and Gonam, over the Stanovoy range, down the Zeya and Amur to its mouth, then along the Okhotsk coast and back by the Maya.
notes: Accounts by Poyarkov's men record Daur and Nivkh (Gilyak) peoples along the river.

label: Tasman 2
summary: Charted the north coast of Australia from Cape York round the Gulf of Carpentaria and Arnhem Land to the north-west coast, as one continuous New Holland.

label: Dezhnev
summary: Sailed from the Kolyma round the eastern tip of Asia through the strait later named for Bering, proving Asia and America were separated.
notes: Report lay in Yakutsk archives until Muller found it in 1736, so Europe learned of it only in the 18th century. Wreck site south of the Anadyr uncertain (Cape Navarin area assumed).

label: Dezhnev on foot
summary: Survivors walked from the wreck to the Anadyr mouth and went upriver to found winter quarters near Anadyrsk.

label: Raposo Tavares
summary: Bandeira from Sao Paulo across the Paraguay basin to the Andes foothills and down the Madeira and Amazon.
notes: Route reconstructed and disputed; fetched page confirms only the overall Sao Paulo to Amazon-mouth journey.

label: Khabarov
summary: Up the Olyokma and Tungir to the Shilka and Amur, built Albazin and sailed down the Amur past the Sungari to near modern Khabarovsk.
notes: Return trip to Yakutsk in 1650 to raise reinforcements omitted.

label: Stadukhin overland
summary: Opened the overland route from the Kolyma via the Anyuy to the Anadyr, then reached the Penzhina and followed the north coast of the Sea of Okhotsk to Okhotsk.
notes: Penzhina to Taui partly by boat along the coast.

leader: Hendrick Hamel and the Sperwer crew
label: Hamel
summary: Shipwrecked Dutch sailors held in Korea for 13 years; Hamel's journal was Europe's first first-hand account of Joseon Korea.
notes: Source page could not be fetched in this session (web search budget exhausted); dates and route from general knowledge, check before publication.

label: Grueber
summary: Peking to Agra by Xining, the Kokonor and Lhasa, then over the Himalaya to Kathmandu, the first Europeans in Lhasa.
notes: 214-day journey; d'Orville died at Agra. Grueber returned to Rome via Persia and Turkey in 1664.

label: Evliya Celebi: Vienna
summary: Accompanied Kara Mehmed Pasha's embassy to Vienna and described the Habsburg capital in the Seyahatname.
notes: His further claimed travels to the Netherlands and Scandinavia are doubted.

label: Evliya Celebi: Nile
summary: Travelled up the Nile through Ottoman Egypt and Nubia towards the Funj sultanate of Sennar.
notes: Sudan and Ethiopian sections of the Seyahatname are hard to verify.

label: Marquette and Jolliet
summary: Down the Fox-Wisconsin route and the Mississippi to the Arkansas mouth, proving the river drains to the Gulf.
notes: Five voyageurs; Miami and Illinois guides on the Fox-Wisconsin portage.

label: Le Griffon
summary: First sailing ship on the upper Great Lakes, through Lakes Erie, Huron and Michigan to Green Bay.

label: La Salle
summary: Descended the Illinois and Mississippi to the Gulf of Mexico and claimed Louisiana for France.
notes: Henri de Tonti and Mahican and Abenaki companions; reached the mouth 9 April 1682.

label: Atlasov
summary: First systematic Russian exploration of Kamchatka, from Anadyrsk down both coasts and the Kamchatka river to the Golygina.
notes: Party included about 60 Yukaghirs; Itelmen allies guided them on the Kamchatka. Met the shipwrecked Japanese Denbei, Russia's first Japanese contact.

label: Dampier
summary: Surveyed Shark Bay and the north-west coast of Australia, then found New Britain and the strait between it and New Guinea.
notes: His 1688 Cygnet visit to King Sound is not separately mapped.

label: Tulisen to the Kalmyks
summary: Qing embassy across Mongolia and Siberia to Ayuka Khan of the Kalmyks on the lower Volga; described in Yiyu lu (1723).
notes: Siberian route via Irkutsk, Tomsk, Tobolsk and Kazan reconstructed in outline.

label: Desideri
summary: Delhi to Kashmir, Ladakh and across western Tibet past Kailash to Lhasa, followed by the fullest early European study of Tibet.
notes: Crossed the plateau with the caravan of a Mongol princess (Casal); Kailash and Tsangpo route points assumed. Dakpo stay 1717.

leader: Kangxi atlas survey (Huangyu Quanlan Tu, base-like)
label: Kangxi atlas
summary: Jesuit and Chinese survey of the whole Qing realm (1708 to 1717), with lama surveyors mapping Tibet to Mount Kailash and Lake Manasarovar.
notes: Jesuits Jean-Baptiste Regis, Pierre Jartoux and others; Tibet was surveyed by trained lamas (1711 to 1717).

label: Messerschmidt
summary: First scientific expedition through Siberia, from Tobolsk via Tomsk, the Yenisei and Lower Tunguska to Irkutsk and Dauria.
notes: Swedish prisoner Philip Johan von Strahlenberg accompanied him early on and published a map of Siberia (1730). Return to St Petersburg 1727-28.

label: Qing to Lhasa
summary: Qing armies from Kokonor and Sichuan expelled the Dzungars and occupied Lhasa.
notes: A second column marched from Sichuan via Batang and Chamdo.

label: Desideri return
summary: Left Lhasa by Kuti on the Nepal border and returned via the Ganges plain to Agra.
notes: Only Kuti and Agra named in the source.

label: Roggeveen
summary: Found Easter Island (5 April 1722), islands of the Tuamotus and Society group (Bora Bora, Maupiti) and Samoa.
notes: Route past New Guinea is summarised in the source; the north-coast track is reconstructed.

label: Bering 1
summary: First Kamchatka Expedition: sailed north along Kamchatka and Chukotka through the Bering Strait to 67 18 N.
notes: Specific page listed but not fetched in this session (search budget exhausted); route and dates from compiler's general knowledge.

leader: Johann Georg Gmelin and Gerhard Friedrich Muller
label: Gmelin and Muller
sponsor: Russian Academy of Sciences (Great Northern Expedition)
summary: Academic land party of the Great Northern Expedition, surveying western and southern Siberia, Baikal and Dauria before reaching Yakutsk.
notes: Gmelin's Flora Sibirica and Muller's archive work (which found Dezhnev's report) followed.

leader: Murillo Velarde map of the Philippines
label: Philippines
summary: The first scientific map of the Philippines, 1734.
notes: Survey and settlement layer: the region lights in this year. Date from general knowledge; the cited pages were not read for this layer.

leader: Jesuit surveyors for the Kangxi Emperor (Regis, Jartoux, Fridelli and others)
label: Kangxi atlas
summary: The Jesuit-Qing triangulation survey of China, Manchuria and Korea (1708-1718) reached European readers through Du Halde (1735) and d'Anville's atlas, replacing guesswork with measured maps.
notes: Base-like entry: start set to 1735, when Du Halde printed the maps in Paris (atlas made in China 1718-19). Korea drawn from Korean maps, not surveyed. Tibet section (from lama surveyors, 1717) not included here.

label: Malygin
summary: Western detachment of the Great Northern Expedition: charted the Kara Sea coast from the Pechora past Yamal to the Ob estuary.
notes: Linked to Ovtsyn's Ob to Yenisei survey (1737 to 1738). Specific page listed but not fetched in this session (search budget exhausted); route and dates from compiler's general knowledge.

label: Krasheninnikov
sponsor: Russian Academy of Sciences (Great Northern Expedition)
summary: Spent four years exploring Kamchatka; his Description of Kamchatka (1755) was Europe's first full account of the peninsula and its Itelmen people.
notes: Okhotsk to Bolsheretsk by sea. Source page could not be fetched in this session (web search budget exhausted); dates and route from general knowledge, check before publication.
